project.title: Lysinoalanine crosslinking is a conserved post-translational modification in the spirochete flagellar hookLysinoalanine crosslinking is a conserved post-translational modification in the spirochete flagellar hook
project.projectDescription: In this project, we investigated whether diverse spirochete species contain lysinoalanine cross-linkages between conserved residues in their flagellar hook proteins (FlgE). We examined the following species: Treponema denticola¸ Borreliella burgdorferi, Treponema phagedenis, Treponema pallidum, Brachyspira hyodysenteriae, Leptospira interrogans. For each bacterial species, we examined a variety of different sample types, including recombinantly produced FlgE, polyhooks purified from flik knock-out strains, and wild-type periplasmic filaments. Overall, our data suggests that lysinoalanine crosslinking in a conserved FlgE post-translational modification in spirochetes and is required for the unique motility of these organisms. For more information, please see the following manuscript: https://doi.org/10.1101/2023.06.13.544825.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Samples were enriched by running isolated samples on a 4-20% SDS-PAGE gel and collecting the upper region of the stacking portion of the gels for MS/MS analysis. Samples were mixed with SDS loading dye (1x final concentration) and excess reducing agent, heated at 85C for 5 minutes, and then electrophoresed. Gels were then stained with Coomassie blue protein stain, destained, and the gels rinsed in distilled-deionized water to remove excess destain. Bands were then excised from the gel and submitted to MS. For more information regarding materials and methods, please see the following manuscript: https://doi.org/10.1101/2023.06.13.544825.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: All the raw files were manully checked for b/y, c/z ions of the target crosslinked peptides.
